claims.text: Pre-depositing a thin, conformal Cu coating on W particles by ALD before consolidation will create a uniform nanoscale Cu interlayer at W–Cu interfaces.
The nanoscale Cu interlayer will promote intimate metallurgical bonding between W and Cu.
The ALD-deposited Cu layer will enhance Cu wettability on W during sintering.
The ALD-deposited Cu layer will enhance W–Cu interdiffusion during sintering.
Enhanced wettability and interdiffusion will reduce or eliminate interfacial void formation.
Enhanced wettability and interdiffusion will minimize phase separation at W–Cu interfaces.
Reduced interfacial void content and more intimate W–Cu contact will lower interfacial thermal resistance.
Lower interfacial thermal resistance will improve composite thermal conductivity relative to direct Cu infiltration or uncoated sintering.
The ALD-treated composite will maintain or improve mechanical durability relative to conventionally infiltrated or sintered W–Cu composites.
Conventional direct Cu infiltration, spark-plasma sintering, or mechanical-alloying routes typically yield voids and phase separation in W–Cu composites.
Using processing temperatures below the Cu boiling point will avoid Cu boiling during consolidation.
An inert or reducing processing atmosphere will prevent oxidation.
Fusion-reactor service exposes relevant components to high temperatures, large heat loads, energetic plasma species, and neutron irradiation.
W can suffer brittle failure and irradiation-associated surface damage under fusion-relevant conditions, making mechanical durability a relevant service constraint.
ALD may be difficult to scale while retaining uniform coverage over complex W geometries.
The long-term adhesion of the deposited Cu layer may be unstable under cyclic thermal and irradiation exposure.
